issues.legal_issue: The location where profits from sales of unascertained goods arise depends on when and where property in the goods passes to the buyer.
material_facts: The goods were sold under contracts on F.O.B. terms, with payment of a specified portion of the provisional invoice available against shipping documents and the balance payable after weighment and assay at destination.

The seller shipped the goods under bills of lading issued in its own name and endorsed the bills in blank, but the documents were not delivered to the buyers’ bank until the buyers’ bank accepted the bill of exchange.
The buyers’ bank accepted the bill of exchange and received the bill of lading and invoice from the seller’s agent in London.
The parties treated the place of sale as the place where the income arose.
issues.conclusion: The property in the goods could not have passed before acceptance of the bill of exchange and delivery of the documents in London; the sales took place outside British India, so the profits arose outside British India.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4, 18, 23 and 25 of the Indian Sale of Goods Act, a sale of unascertained goods requires ascertainment and unconditional appropriation, and a seller may reserve the right of disposal until specified conditions are fulfilled. F.O.B. delivery and the passing of risk are relevant but not decisive if the seller retains control through the documents of title. Under section 4 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the agreed location of the sales determined where the profits arose. The court relied on The Prinz Adalbert, [1917] A.C. 586, in explaining the effect of negotiating a bill of exchange with a bill of lading as security.

predicates.income_tax_profit_accrual_location_case: The proceeding determines where profits from sales arose for income-tax purposes.
predicates.goods_unascertained: The contracts concerned goods that had not been ascertained when the contracts were made.
predicates.seller_retained_documents_until_draft_ac: The seller kept control of the documents of title until the buyer’s bank accepted the bill of exchange.
predicates.title_documents_delivered_outside_tax_te: The seller’s agent delivered the documents of title to the buyer’s bank outside the relevant tax territory.
predicates.profits_arose_outside_tax_territory: The profits from the sales arose outside the relevant tax territory.

issues.definition: When an income-tax proceeding concerns profits from unascertained goods and the seller retains the documents of title until the buyer’s bank accepts the draft and receives those documents outside the tax territory, the profits arise outside that territory.

issues.legal_issue: The location where sale proceeds are first received depends on whether a payment in the seller’s territory is a receipt of the price or merely an advance from the seller’s own bank.
material_facts: The seller’s bank in Madras credited the seller with the amount of bills of exchange after receiving the bills and shipping documents from the seller.
The seller’s bank in Madras and its London bank were agents of the seller, not of the buyers.
The London bank presented the bills to the buyers’ banks, received payment there, and received the balance of the price there after weighment and assay.
The Madras bank’s credit to the seller was an advance secured by the goods and the seller’s liability on the bills, rather than payment of the price by or on behalf of the buyers.
Later adjustments in the London bank’s books did not constitute receipt of the profits in British India.
issues.conclusion: The Madras bank’s credit was an advance and not receipt of the price; the price was first received by the seller’s agent in London, so the profits were received outside British India.
issues.legal_principle: For the receipt inquiry under section 4 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a credit from the seller’s own bank is not receipt of the sale price where it is an advance against security and the bank is not acting for the buyer. The price is received where the buyer’s bank pays it to the seller’s agent. The court relied on The Prinz Adalbert, [1917] A.C. 586, for the nature of a banker’s advance made against a bill of exchange and bill of lading.

predicates.income_tax_profit_receipt_location_case: The proceeding determines where profits from sales were received for income-tax purposes.
predicates.local_bank_credit_was_seller_advance: A bank in the seller’s territory credited the seller with funds as an advance secured by the goods and the seller’s liability on a bill, rather than as payment by or for the buyer.
predicates.buyer_bank_paid_seller_agent_outside_tax: The buyer’s bank paid the sale proceeds to the seller’s agent outside the relevant tax territory.
predicates.balance_received_by_seller_agent_outside: The seller’s agent received the balance of the sale price outside the relevant tax territory.
predicates.profits_were_first_received_outside_tax_: The profits from the sales were first received outside the relevant tax territory.

issues.definition: When a local bank’s credit is only an advance to the seller and the buyer’s bank pays the proceeds and balance to the seller’s agent outside the tax territory, the profits are first received outside that territory.
